evals.prompt: Validate GOFR Splunk dashboards from the paas-splunk-object-backup repository. Main dashboard is at ~/github/paas-splunk-object-backup/nobody/fs-turbo/data/ui/views/gofr_dashboard.xml. Use field mappings from the analyze report at ~/github/gofr/.claude/analyze-reports/05-field-naming-analysis.md. Generate validation report and Dynatrace DQL equivalents.
evals.expected_output: Complete validation report showing: (1) Splunk app identified (fs-turbo), (2) Service filtered to 'gofr', (3) Query types distinguished (metrics vs logs), (4) Field validation with GREEN/YELLOW/RED risk assessment, (5) Dynatrace DQL equivalents for all application log queries, (6) Scope statement about 'nobody' directory only

assertions.name: Report includes Splunk app context (fs-turbo)
assertions.description: Validation report should mention the Splunk application name (fs-turbo) to establish context

assertions.name: Distinguishes metrics from log queries
assertions.description: Report should note that most panels are metrics queries (not affected) and only validate application log queries

assertions.name: Uses GREEN/YELLOW/RED risk criteria
assertions.description: Risk assessment should use the defined color-coded levels with clear definitions

assertions.name: Includes Dynatrace DQL equivalents
assertions.description: Each validated query should have a corresponding DQL translation

assertions.name: States scope limitation (nobody directory)
assertions.description: Report should explicitly state that only shared objects in 'nobody' directory are validated

assertions.name: Validates business event routing
assertions.description: Should check logback configuration for business event routing to separate file

evals.prompt: I'm migrating the 'watch' service to structured logging. The Splunk app is fs-turbo which has 46 dashboards total. Can you validate just the watch-related dashboards? The backup is at ~/github/paas-splunk-object-backup/nobody/fs-turbo/. Field mappings are at ~/github/gofr/.claude/analyze-reports/05-field-naming-analysis.md (use as example - watch may have different fields).
evals.expected_output: Skill should: (1) Ask user to confirm Splunk app name (fs-turbo), (2) List total dashboards (46), (3) Filter to service-specific dashboards using 'watch' pattern, (4) List matching dashboards before validation, (5) Explain that filtering reduces scope, (6) Generate report for filtered dashboards only

assertions.name: Prompts for Splunk app confirmation
assertions.description: Should explicitly ask for or confirm the Splunk application name

assertions.name: Reports total dashboard count
assertions.description: Should count and report total dashboards in the app (46 for fs-turbo)

assertions.name: Filters by service pattern
assertions.description: Should use grep or similar to filter dashboards matching 'watch'

assertions.name: Lists filtered results before validating
assertions.description: Should show user which dashboards match the filter and ask for confirmation

assertions.name: Explains filtering rationale
assertions.description: Should explain that filtering focuses validation on relevant dashboards

evals.prompt: Validate Splunk alerts for the 'gofr' service in fs-turbo app. The alerts are in ~/github/paas-splunk-object-backup/nobody/fs-turbo/savedsearches.conf. I need to know if any alert queries will break after migrating to structured logging. Field mappings at ~/github/gofr/.claude/analyze-reports/05-field-naming-analysis.md.
evals.expected_output: Skill should: (1) Read savedsearches.conf, (2) Count total saved searches, (3) Filter to gofr-specific alerts, (4) Parse alert SPL queries, (5) Validate field references same as dashboard queries, (6) Report which alerts are affected (if any), (7) Include alert-specific considerations (suppress fields, email actions)

assertions.name: Reads savedsearches.conf
assertions.description: Should locate and parse the savedsearches.conf file

assertions.name: Counts total saved searches
assertions.description: Should report total number of saved searches in the file (145 for fs-turbo)

assertions.name: Filters to service-specific alerts
assertions.description: Should filter to alerts matching 'gofr' pattern

assertions.name: Parses alert SPL queries
assertions.description: Should extract 'search =' field from alert stanzas

assertions.name: Validates alert field references
assertions.description: Should apply same field validation as dashboard queries

assertions.name: Reports alert-specific metadata
assertions.description: Should note alert severity, suppression fields, or email actions if relevant
